meta.titre: Macroeconomic Policy Objectives: aims, indicators and conflicts
meta.sous_theme: Main government objectives, reasons for intervention and conflicts between aims

sections.contenu_markdown: Every year the government of Cameroon adopts a budget, and every household feels the results: whether young graduates find work, whether the price of food and fuel stays bearable, whether the roads and schools improve. Behind such choices lie a small number of macroeconomic aims that governments everywhere pursue. The difficulty is that the aims do not always fit together, so choosing between them is the heart of economic policy. At A Level you are asked to list and define the objectives, to give reasons for intervention, and to explain why they sometimes conflict.

items: Gross domestic product (GDP) is the total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year.
Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level, measured by the change in a price index.
Exports are goods and services sold abroad, and imports are goods and services bought from abroad.

sections.titre: The main macroeconomic objectives and why governments intervene
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Main objectives

| Objective | Meaning | Indicator |
|---|---|---|
| Low unemployment (full employment) | Those willing and able to work can find jobs; some frictional and structural unemployment remains | Unemployed divided by the labour force, times 100 |
| Price stability | Low and stable inflation | Percentage change in a price index |
| Economic growth | A sustained rise in real output | Percentage change in real GDP |
| Balance of payments equilibrium | Receipts from abroad roughly match payments abroad over time | Current account balance |
| Fair distribution of income | Less poverty and extreme inequality | Income shares of rich and poor groups |
| Sustainable development | Growth that protects the environment for the future | Indicators of pollution and resource depletion |

### Why governments intervene
Markets alone may not reach these aims. The reasons for intervention include: to provide public goods such as roads and defence; to correct externalities such as pollution; to ensure enough merit goods such as education and health, and to discourage demerit goods; to control monopoly power and protect consumers; to reduce poverty and inequality; to stabilise the economy when output, prices or employment fluctuate; and to diversify an economy that depends heavily on exports of a few primary products, which exposes it to price swings. The government also builds infrastructure and creates a stable climate for investment.

### Instruments
**Fiscal policy** (taxation and government spending), **monetary policy** (the money supply and interest rates; in Cameroon it is set for the CEMAC area by the BEAC), **supply-side policy** (education, training, infrastructure) and direct controls.

### Conflicts between objectives
| Conflict | Reason |
|---|---|
| Low unemployment and price stability | Higher demand creates jobs but also pulls prices up (see the Phillips curve) |
| Growth and the balance of payments | Higher incomes increase spending on imports |
| Growth and the environment | More production may mean more pollution and resource use |
| Equity and growth | High taxes on the rich may weaken incentives |

A government usually ranks the aims according to its circumstances, so it is wise to say which objective is the priority and why.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command is state, list or name
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name each objective in a short, exact phrase, such as "price stability" or "balance of payments equilibrium", and add a brief explanation if marks allow. When the question says "apart from low unemployment", do not repeat unemployment. For a list of reasons for intervention, give distinct points such as public goods, externalities, merit goods, monopoly control, inequality and stabilisation, not five wordings of the same idea.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When data are given and a calculation is needed
variantes.contenu_markdown: Unemployment rate $= \dfrac{\text{unemployed}}{\text{labour force}} \times 100$. Inflation rate $= \dfrac{\text{new index} - \text{old index}}{\text{old index}} \times 100$. Real GDP $= \dfrac{\text{nominal GDP}}{\text{price index}} \times 100$, and growth is the percentage change in real GDP. Current account balance $=$ exports $-$ imports of goods and services, plus net income and transfers; in simple questions, exports $-$ imports. State the unit (per cent or billion FCFA).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command is discuss, assess or to what extent
variantes.contenu_markdown: Explain each conflict with a chain of cause and effect, then judge how serious it is. Conflicts may be reduced by supply-side policy, which raises output without extra inflation, or may matter less when the economy has spare capacity. The priority depends on the situation: a country with high inflation may put price stability first, one with severe unemployment may put jobs first. Finish with a reasoned judgement.

sections.enonce_markdown:
The table gives hypothetical figures for a country over two years.

| | Year 1 | Year 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Labour force | 6,000,000 | 6,000,000 |
| Unemployed | 480,000 | 420,000 |
| Real GDP (billion FCFA) | 18,000 | 18,900 |
| Consumer price index | 125 | 130 |
| Exports (billion FCFA) | 4,000 | 4,200 |
| Imports (billion FCFA) | 4,400 | 4,900 |

(a) Calculate the unemployment rate in each year, the rate of growth, the rate of inflation in year 2 and the trade balance in each year.
(b) State which objectives improved and which got worse.
(c) Explain the conflict that the figures illustrate.

etapes.justification: The rate is the unemployed as a percentage of the labour force.
Growth is the percentage change in real GDP.
Inflation is the percentage change in the price index.

etapes.action: Calculate the trade balance in each year.
etapes.justification: The balance is exports minus imports.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Year 1: $4\,000 - 4\,400 = -400$. Year 2: $4\,200 - 4\,900 = -700$. The deficit widened from 400 to 700 billion FCFA.

etapes.justification: Compare each result with the aim of a high or low value.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Unemployment fell (improved). Growth of 5 per cent is positive. Inflation of 4 per cent is fairly low. The trade deficit widened (worse).

etapes.justification: Imports grew by about 11.4 per cent while exports grew by 5 per cent.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Faster growth raised incomes and jobs but also raised spending on imports, so growth and the fall in unemployment worsened the balance of payments.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Unemployment 8 per cent then 7 per cent; growth 5 per cent; inflation 4 per cent; trade balance -400 then -700 billion FCFA. (b) Unemployment and growth improved, inflation stayed low, and the trade balance worsened. (c) Growth conflicts with balance of payments equilibrium, because higher incomes raise imports faster than exports.

items.erreur_markdown: "Full employment means that nobody is unemployed."
items.pourquoi_faux: Some unemployment always exists, for example workers between jobs (frictional) or without the skills demanded (structural).
items.correction_markdown: Full employment means that everyone who is willing and able to work at the going wage can find a job, apart from frictional and structural unemployment.

items.erreur_markdown: "Price stability means that prices never change."
items.pourquoi_faux: Price stability is a low and stable rate of inflation. Prices may still rise slowly.
items.correction_markdown: The aim is low, stable inflation, and avoiding deflation as well as high inflation.

items.erreur_markdown: "Economic growth means that nominal GDP has risen."
items.pourquoi_faux: Nominal GDP can rise only because prices have risen. Growth refers to a rise in real output.
items.correction_markdown: Economic growth is a rise in real GDP, found by removing the effect of price changes.

items.erreur_markdown: "A balance of payments deficit means that government spending is larger than tax revenue."
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes a budget deficit. The balance of payments records a country's dealings with the rest of the world.
items.correction_markdown: A balance of payments deficit means that payments abroad exceed receipts from abroad, for example imports larger than exports on the current account.

items.erreur_markdown: "A government can easily achieve all its macroeconomic objectives at the same time."
items.pourquoi_faux: Objectives often conflict: policies that reduce unemployment may raise inflation or imports.
items.correction_markdown: Explain at least one conflict, such as growth and the balance of payments, and say how the government might choose between the aims.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) For each indicator state the objective it measures: (i) the change in the consumer price index; (ii) the unemployment rate; (iii) the change in real GDP; (iv) the current account balance.
(b) A country has a labour force of 5,000,000 and 350,000 unemployed. Calculate the unemployment rate.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) (i) **price stability**; (ii) **low unemployment (full employment)**; (iii) **economic growth**; (iv) **balance of payments equilibrium**.
(b) $350\,000 \div 5\,000\,000 \times 100 = 7$: the rate is **7 per cent**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A country's nominal GDP is 30,000 billion FCFA in year 1 and 33,600 billion FCFA in year 2. The GDP deflator is 120 in year 1 and 128 in year 2.
(a) Calculate real GDP in each year, using real GDP = nominal GDP divided by the deflator, times 100.
(b) Calculate the rate of growth of nominal GDP and of real GDP.
(c) Calculate the rate of inflation as measured by the deflator, to one decimal place.
(d) Explain why a government should look at real GDP when it assesses growth.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Year 1: $30\,000 \div 120 \times 100 = 25\,000$. Year 2: $33\,600 \div 128 \times 100 = 26\,250$. Real GDP is **25,000 and 26,250 billion FCFA**.
(b) Nominal: $(33\,600 - 30\,000) \div 30\,000 \times 100 = 12$ per cent. Real: $(26\,250 - 25\,000) \div 25\,000 \times 100 = 5$ per cent. The rates are **12 per cent and 5 per cent**.
(c) $(128 - 120) \div 120 \times 100 = 6.7$: **6.7 per cent**.
(d) Nominal GDP rose by 12 per cent, but more than half of that rise was caused by higher prices. Only real GDP shows the extra output that raises living standards.

items.enonce_markdown:
A government wants faster growth and a balanced current account. Suppose that every extra 1,000 billion FCFA of national income raises imports by 250 billion FCFA, and exports do not change.
(a) Calculate the marginal propensity to import.
(b) By how much does the current account balance worsen if national income rises by 4,000 billion FCFA?
(c) Discuss to what extent a government can achieve growth and balance of payments equilibrium together. (8 marks)
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $250 \div 1\,000 = 0.25$: the marginal propensity to import is **0.25**.
(b) $0.25 \times 4\,000 = 1\,000$: the balance worsens by **1,000 billion FCFA**.
(c) Award marks for: higher income raises imports, so growth tends to worsen the balance (2); the conflict is stronger if the country imports many capital and consumer goods (1); it is weaker if growth is led by exports or if domestic substitutes for imports are produced (2); supply-side policy can improve competitiveness and raise exports (1); the fixed link of the CFA franc to the euro and a regional monetary policy limit the instruments available (1); a reasoned conclusion that the aims can be reconciled only partly or in the longer term (1).

items_markdown: The main objectives are low unemployment, price stability, economic growth and balance of payments equilibrium, with fair income distribution and sustainable development as further aims.
Governments intervene to provide public goods, correct externalities, supply merit goods, control monopoly, reduce inequality and stabilise the economy.
Each objective has an indicator: unemployment rate, change in a price index, change in real GDP, and the current account balance.
Objectives conflict: lower unemployment against price stability, growth against the balance of payments, and growth against the environment.
In evaluation, say which objective is the priority in the situation and why, and how supply-side policy may ease the conflict.
